slides.headline: Her parents emigrated from India in 1960. In 2026, Forbes named her one of the world's top innovators at 59.
Maya Ajmera, CEO of the Society for Science, was named to Forbes' 2026 '50 Over 50' Innovation list
slides.body: Produced with Mika Brzezinski's Know Your Value initiative, the sixth annual list honours 200 women across four categories - Ajmera featured among the Innovation honourees.

slides.headline: Before leading the organization that publishes Science News, she spent nearly two decades building a nonprofit for children.
slides.body: From 1993 to 2011, she founded and led the Global Fund for Children, directing private philanthropic capital to community-based organizations supporting vulnerable children and youth worldwide, before becoming President and CEO of the Society for Science & the Public.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits when the children of its diaspora end up leading the institutions that shape global science journalism and youth STEM.
slides.body: Ajmera's path - from a neuroscience degree to running a century-old science publication - shows a second-generation Indian American reaching the top of a field entirely removed from her parents' own careers.
